newsitem.title: UK: Charter says Howden to enhance earnings.
newsitem.headline: Charter says Howden to enhance earnings.

text.p: British engineering group Charter Plc said on Friday that the acquisition of Howden Group Plc would boost earnings in its first year.
Charter chairman and chief executive Jeffrey Herbert told a news conference "I believe the acquisition will be earnings enhancing in the first full year."

Earlier, Charter said it had made an agreed offer for Howden valuing the company at around 378 million stg. Herbert said cost savings would come from rationalisation and efficiency gains, and added, "we think we can add value to Howden."

Herbert said Howden's Air and Gas Handling division, which makes ventilation fans for industrial use including mines and tunnels as well as pumps and cooling systems, was the "one gorgeous centre" of Howden's business.

The division made operating profits of 26.6 million stg in the year to April 1996 on sales of 328 million stg, accounting for 72 percent of Howden's total operating profit and 69 percent of turnover. Herbert said the other two divisions, which make drilling and boring equipment and packaging and handling equipment, "need to be reviewed an certainly we will be doing that in the early days."
Herbert said Charter's aim was "to have three strong manufacturing businesses that are market leaders and this will be the basis of Charter's future growth".

Charter, which has shifted radically from being a mining and industrial group to a pure engineering concern, is centred on the welding products operation Esab, which it bought in 1994 for 445 million stg. Its second business is the Pandrol rail track equipment operation based in Britain and the U.S.
Charter, which approached Howden about a bid on Monday after its interest was leaked to the press, said its profit margins of 10.5 percent compared with Howden's 7.9 percent.

"Charter today is about world market-leading businesses, quite simply because market leaders earn larger margins than market followers. Howden is an exception because as a world leader it earns smaller margins than its competitors," Herbert said, adding that "some of their competitors would appear to make margins forty to fifty percent higher."
In its central ventilation operations, Howden's main global competitors are ABB Flakt of Sweden and Germany's Deutsche Babcock AG.

Charter said Howden's percentage share of the world market for large ventilation fans was "into the upper twenties" with an overall market share of around 20 percent, compared with around 15 percent for ABB Flakt, its next largest competitor.
